title: Find the year in which the maximum number of employees joined.
shortTitle: Find the year in which the maximum number of employees joined
keyPoints: groupingBy(e -> e.getJoinDate().getYear(), counting()) produces Map<Integer, Long> of joins per year
max(comparingByValue()) finds the year with the most joins
This is the standard group-count-max pattern applied to a date component
Handle ties if multiple years have the same max count
getYear() extracts the year component from a LocalDate
Sort the result by year for a chronological hiring trend report

s1_definition.oneliner: Group by the year component of the joining date with counting(), then find the max entry by value.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **groupingBy(e -> e.getJoinDate().getYear(), counting())** produces `Map<Integer, Long>` of joins per year.
- **max(comparingByValue())** on the entrySet finds the peak hiring year.
- Same **group-count-max** pattern as department and city questions.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank's annual report asks: 'In which year did we hire the most people?' Count joiners per year, then find the peak year.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Finding the peak hiring year uses groupingBy with the year extracted from the join date as the classifier and counting as the downstream, then max by value. Collect to a TreeMap for chronological display.

Remember one sentence: groupingBy(joinYear, counting()) then max by value finds the year with the most hires.
